## Questions 

Q1. How many rows are in penguins? How many columns?

A1. I can see the rows and columns when viewing the data frame. Or by calling specific R functions

```{r}
penguins
```

Base R functions

```{r}
nrow(penguins)
ncol(penguins)
```


Q2. What does the bill_depth_mm variable in the penguins data frame describe? Read the help for ?penguins to find out.

A2: Done. We can also review details at the package website which is listed in the package help file. (?palmerpenguins)

![From the package website](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/reference/figures/culmen_depth.png)

Q3. Make a scatterplot of bill_depth_mm vs. bill_length_mm. That is, make a scatterplot with bill_depth_mm on the y-axis and bill_length_mm on the x-axis. Describe the relationship between these two variables.

A3. I don't see a strong linear relationship; however, there does appear to be clustering in the data.

```{r}
ggplot(data = penguins) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = bill_length_mm, y = bill_depth_mm))
```


Q4. What happens if you make a scatterplot of species vs. bill_depth_mm? What might be a better choice of geom?

A4. See the plots below: 

```{r}
ggplot(data = penguins) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = bill_depth_mm, y = species))
```


```{r}
ggplot(data = penguins) +
  geom_boxplot(mapping = aes(x = bill_depth_mm, y = species))
```

```{r}
ggplot(data = penguins) +
  geom_violin(mapping = aes(x = bill_depth_mm, y = species))
```


Q5. Why does the following give an error and how would you fix it?

```r
ggplot(data = penguins) + 
  geom_point()
```

A5. We need to map asethetics to the plot; either inside the ggplot() function or the geom_point() function.

```{r}
ggplot(data = penguins) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = bill_depth_mm))
```

Q6. What does the na.rm argument do in geom_point()? What is the default value of the argument? Create a scatterplot where you successfully use this argument set to TRUE.

A6. `na.rm` removes the warning message.  

From the documentation, we can see the default value is FALSE

```r
Usage
geom_point(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  stat = "identity",
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)
```

Code with `na.rm = TRUE`

```{r}
ggplot(data = penguins) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = bill_depth_mm), na.rm = TRUE)
```


Q7. Add the following caption to the plot you made in the previous exercise: “Data come from the palmerpenguins package.” Hint: Take a look at the documentation for labs().

A7. See code below

```{r}
ggplot(data = penguins) + 
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = bill_depth_mm), na.rm = TRUE) +
  labs(
    caption = "my caption"
  )
```

Q8. Recreate the following visualization. What aesthetic should bill_depth_mm be mapped to? And should it be mapped at the global level or at the geom level?

![title of the chart](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/data-visualize_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-16-1.png)

A8. See code below

```{r}
ggplot(data = penguins, mapping = aes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = body_mass_g)) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(color = bill_depth_mm)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = "y ~ x")
```


From the "ALT TEXT" of the book figure: A scatterplot of body mass vs. flipper length of penguins, colored  by bill depth. A smooth curve of the relationship between body mass  and flipper length is overlaid. The relationship is positive,  fairly linear, and moderately strong.

Q9. Run this code in your head and predict what the output will look like. Then, run the code in R and check your predictions.

```r
ggplot(
  data = penguins,
  mapping = aes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = body_mass_g, color = island)
) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE)
```

A9. Scatter plot with a smooth "loess" line for each island. Points are color coded by island. The confidence interval is removed.

```{r}
ggplot(
  data = penguins,
  mapping = aes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = body_mass_g, color = island)
) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE)
```

Q10. Will these two graphs look different? Why/why not?

```r
ggplot(
  data = penguins,
  mapping = aes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = body_mass_g)
) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth()

ggplot() +
  geom_point(
    data = penguins,
    mapping = aes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = body_mass_g)
  ) +
  geom_smooth(
    data = penguins,
    mapping = aes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = body_mass_g)
  )
```

A10. The plots will look the same. The aesthetics are mapped the same; the first ggplot is just more concise. 

```{r}
ggplot(
  data = penguins,
  mapping = aes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = body_mass_g)
) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth()

ggplot() +
  geom_point(
    data = penguins,
    mapping = aes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = body_mass_g)
  ) +
  geom_smooth(
    data = penguins,
    mapping = aes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = body_mass_g)
  )
```
